purpose: Measure the frame component of standalone-fragment versus full-context latent mismatch before any change to training targets.
context: Existing target codes already use whole-protein PCA. Supplied fragment codes use the fragment-only PCA frame. The original288training conditions differ by median141.3degrees; this does not prove an accuracy limitation. Anchoring targets changes the inherited convention and is not a missing-preprocessing correction.
selection: Only original32training proteins. Sort(length,id), take indices0,4,...28; eight families. For each use existing f30_left, f30_center, f30_right:24conditions. No development or locked-test scoring.
intervention: Fit one proper global CA transform from the native target fragment to the already supplied standalone fragment coordinates, then apply it to every backbone atom before encoding. Require all supplied fragment atoms to match<=1e-4. No3x3 transform is applied to latent channels. All input features and original target labels remain preserved.
measurement: Compare motif-position latent RMSE to supplied standalone codes before versus after anchoring. Re-encode original backbones to check cached-target parity<=.05RMSE; encode anchored targets and decode both recipes with identical AE3 noise, seed2026100245. Save all24paired latent/reconstruction outputs. Record full-target latent departure from the cached convention explicitly.
controls: Eight center-fragment controls globally rotate and translate the full target before alignment; recovered coordinates and encoded latents must agree<=1e-4. One10minute RTX diagnostic with frozenAE. All failures retained.
followup_gate: At least20percent reduction in mean motif-position latent RMSE with positive lower paired-family95percent bootstrap bound for before-minus-after. At least23/24anchored AND23/24original reconstructions must each be coarse-valid and have proper global CA RMSD<=.5A. A pass qualifies only a separate target-frame training test, not generation or designability. No frame/threshold sweep.
